message.content:
The first risk is that supply constraints will limit the conversion of demand into revenue. That risk would be confirmed by a failure to meet the raised fourth quarter revenue guidance range of $1.930 billion to $1.950 billion despite management stating that orders are slightly up from the third quarter and that the pipeline continues to grow strongly [D3].

The second risk is that one-time tariff impacts recorded in fiscal year 2026 will not repeat, creating a high comparison bar for future profitability. That risk would be confirmed by a decline in operating margin below the long-term target range of 31% to 32% in the fourth quarter or subsequent periods [D3].

The third risk is that the supply environment remains less flexible than a year ago, acting as a governor on near-term revenue conversion. That risk would be confirmed by a sequential decline in quarterly revenue growth or an inability to sustain $2 billion-plus orders for three consecutive quarters as previously projected [D4].
